title: Federated linear bandits: synchronous two-point feedback and gradient heterogeneity
summary: Multiple clients face separate linear losses and exchange information only at prescribed synchronization rounds. Each client simultaneously queries two values of its current local function, and both query points incur loss. The comparator is one fixed point shared by all clients.

model.instance: There are $M$ clients interacting simultaneously in $\mathbb R^d$ for $T=L_{\mathrm{comm}}R_{\mathrm{comm}}$ rounds each. They synchronize once every $L_{\mathrm{comm}}$ rounds, for $R_{\mathrm{comm}}$ synchronizations. $$f_t^m(x)=\langle g_t^m,x\rangle+b_t^m,\qquad \|g_t^m\|_2\le G.$$ $$f_t(x)=\frac1M\sum_{m=1}^{M}f_t^m(x),\qquad \frac1M\sum_{m=1}^{M}\|\nabla f_t^m(x)-\nabla f_t(x)\|_2^2\le\zeta^2\quad(\forall t,x).$$ The adversary may depend on all past actions and the algorithm, but not on current private randomness. All clients share the same hindsight comparator: $$x^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\|x\|_2\le B}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{m=1}^{M}f_t^m(x).$$

operations.query_signature: Each client simultaneously submits $x_t^{m,1},x_t^{m,2}\in\mathbb R^d$ and receives exact values of the same current local function at both points. The second point cannot depend on the first response. There is no independent measurement noise; variance from randomized directions is part of the estimator analysis. Both query points incur loss. The comparator ball $\{x:\|x\|_2\le B\}$ does not restrict all queries. Inputs $M,d,T,L_{\mathrm{comm}},R_{\mathrm{comm}},G,B,\zeta$ are public. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally. No unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available; any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.
